items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: And it was Benny's brother; and Benny wanted me... he got me the job... And I stayed with him about...oh, four or five months.

ctx.x: blood in their eye. Didn't make any difference. Every one of them, he blew 'em all out. Illinois Jacquet, Don Byas, Ben Webster, Willie Smith, Joe Thomas... Hawk never showed up. He never was in town. But everybody that showed up, he wound up blowin' 'em clear out of the place. And he was practically on his face before they even showed... He used to drink like crazy. He was already four feet off the ground when they showed up sober! Then he'd finish 'em off one by one. Never a bad word about 'em. They all put him…

So then I got my chance. One of the waitresses said that a guy wanted to talk me. And it was Benny's brother; and Benny wanted me. Then Jimmy Maxwell, the first trumpet player with Benny Goodman... Benny and Mel Powell had had a fight, and they were through. So Jimmy Maxwell was a good friend of Ben Webster's, and he talked to him about it, and he got me the job -- Ben told him to get me.

Because they were coming to California to make a picture anyway. So they sent ahead and they got me. And I stayed with him about...oh, four or five months. items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: The guys that worked with Harry James were working a very dangerous job... And the heaviest drinker of the whole band was the leader.

ctx.x: The last time I saw him was when Charlie Barnet brought him into New York with a band he put together, a band here for Basin Street East, and Willie was the only guy he brought with him, you know, to play lead. That was the last time I saw him.

Well, see... The guys that worked with Harry James were working a very dangerous job, because it was the heaviest drinking band, outside of Casa Loma, in the world. And the heaviest drinker of the whole band was the leader. And between that and baseball, hard baseball, you didn't belong in the band. So consequently, Willie just turned into an out-and-out lush. I mean, good Lord, it was terrible. Of course, Lester Young would have drank 'em all out of the room.
And Harry was crazy about baseball.
